subject: System Design
title: The Two Generals Problem
description: Learn The Two Generals Problem in one minute.

hook.text: Two generals must attack simultaneously. They communicate by messenger across enemy territory. Can they ever be sure?

buildup.text: General A sends: 'Attack at dawn.' But the messenger might be captured. A can't know if B got the message.

discovery.text: Even if B sends back a confirmation, that confirmation might be lost. Neither can be 100% certain.

twist.text: This is provably unsolvable over an unreliable channel. No number of messages guarantees agreement.

climax.text: This problem models real distributed systems: you can never be perfectly certain a remote node received your message.

punchline.text: You can't guarantee agreement over an unreliable network.

quiz.question: What does the Two Generals Problem prove?
options: Agreement over unreliable channels is impossible to guarantee
